bullets: Game 3 of a seven-game single-deck session (video 370.5-662.5s), against a Miner / Wall Breakers / Magic Archer / Log cycle-bait opponent with Evolved Bats. Recorded as a loss on the lowest-tower tiebreaker (own {left 1423, right 652} vs enemy {left 1809, right 702} at 656-658s); no explicit result call in the transcript, and the in-game clock OCR failed for the whole video, so all timestamps are video seconds.

The engine is dual-lane cheap pressure: nine Goblin Barrels and six Wall Breakers pairs, deliberately split into opposite lanes so one Log cannot cover both — "Let's go for the Evo barrel then wall breakers opposite lane just to keep up the pressure. He has to log the left and then the right side" (523-527s), and later "we out-cycle this log" (646s).

Wall Breakers are used as a Log magnet before the Barrel, not just as damage — "just to force him to log so he can't go for the Marcher immediately" (430-432s) — and a whiffed pair is still counted a success: "We didn't get any damage, but we forced out a lot of elixir" (580-582s).

Defence is Bomb Tower plus Royal Delivery with Fire Spirit and Ice Spirit as the cheap resets, while Magic Archers are stacked deep behind the King Tower for chip — "I need to start stacking up magic archers" (486s). Ronin is a defence-only body here: all six placements are on his own half or the river row, and he states the limit himself — "Having the Ronan would be nice to clear out Wall Breakers, but outside of that, they won't really do too much" (415-418s).

The weakness the game exposes: the deck's only air answers are Fire Spirit, Royal Delivery and the Magic Archers, and Evolved Bats in the lane opposite his committed defence took the right tower from 4858 (526s) to 652 (640s). "I think we're going to lose our tower to the bats in the opposite lane, to be honest" (632s).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers are both cheap spell-bait win conditions played into opposite lanes to overload a single Log, with Fire Spirit and Ice Spirit as 1-elixir cycle cards behind them.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Two 2-3 elixir win conditions that bait the same small spell force the opponent to answer both lanes with one Log. Ryley plays them on a deliberate alternation — Goblin Barrel one tower, Wall Breakers the other a second or two later — so a Log spent on one side leaves the other free, and the Fire Spirit / Ice Spirit pair keeps the rotation fast enough to out-cycle it. Bomb Tower and Royal Delivery cover the ground and air the cheap cards cannot, and Ronin adds a 5-elixir mini-tank whose parry punishes melee defenders, though in this match he uses it purely defensively. The stacked Magic Archers behind the King Tower turn the deck's spare elixir into piercing chip damage without exposing anything to a counterpush. The list's soft spot is massed air: with only Fire Spirit, Royal Delivery and Magic Archer answering flyers, Evolved Bats in the lane opposite the committed defence can out-trade it.
